syn: host [-aACdlnrsTUwv] [-c class] [-N ndots] [-p port] [-R number] [-t type] [-W wait] [-m flag] [ [-4] | [-6] ] [-v] [-V] {name} [server]

o.en: Specifies the query type.

o.es: Consulta de tipo ANY con salida detallada.
o.en: Equivalent to setting the -v option and asking host to make a query of type ANY.
This option specifies that only IPv4 should be used for query transport. See also the -6 option.
This option specifies that only IPv6 should be used for query transport. See also the -4 option.
The -A ("almost all") option is equivalent to -a, except that RRSIG, NSEC, and NSEC3 records are omitted from the output.
This option specifies the query class, which can be used to lookup HS (Hesiod) or CH (Chaosnet) class resource records. The default class is IN (Internet).

This option indicates that named <#std-iscman-named> should check consistency, meaning that host queries the SOA records for zone name from all the listed authoritative name servers for that zone. The list of name servers is defined by the NS records that are found for the zone.
This option prints debugging traces, and is equivalent to the -v verbose option.

This option tells named <#std-iscman-named> to list the zone, meaning the host command performs a zone transfer of zone name and prints out the NS, PTR, and address records (A/AAAA). Together, the -l -a options print all records in the zone.

This option specifies the number of dots (ndots) that have to be in name for it to be considered absolute. The default value is that defined using the ndots statement in /etc/resolv.conf, or 1 if no ndots statement is present.
This option specifies the port to query on the server. The default is 53.

This option specifies a non-recursive query; setting this option clears the RD (recursion desired) bit in the query. This means that the name server receiving the query does not attempt to resolve name.

This option specifies the number of retries for UDP queries. If number is negative or zero, the number of retries is silently set to 1. The default value is 1, or the value of the attempts option in /etc/resolv.conf, if set.
This option tells named <#std-iscman-named> not to send the query to the next nameserver if any server responds with a SERVFAIL response, which is the reverse of normal stub resolver behavior.

This option specifies TCP or UDP. By default, host uses UDP when making queries; the -T option makes it use a TCP connection when querying the name server. TCP is automatically selected for queries that require it, such as zone transfer (AXFR) requests.
This option sets memory usage debugging: the flag can be record, usage, or trace. The -m option can be specified more than once to set multiple flags.
This option sets verbose output, and is equivalent to the -d debug option. Verbose output can also be enabled by setting the debug option in /etc/resolv.conf.
This option prints the version number and exits.
This option sets "wait forever": the query timeout is set to the maximum possible. See also the -W option.

This options sets the length of the wait timeout, indicating that named <#std-iscman-named> should wait for up to wait seconds for a reply. If wait is less than 1, the wait interval is set to 1 second. By default, host waits for 5 seconds for UDP responses and 10 seconds for TCP connections.
